scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster whose node A restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} long enough for both sides to elect and commit a different entry at the same index and term, and is then healed; this revision samples each node's applied FSM commands after healing in addition to the log payloads.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations only: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter(D), AddVoter(E) and a further apply.

A is shut down gracefully and restarted from its own store objects; all five nodes run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the persisted commit index the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
The partition and the healing are expressed only by transport disconnection and reconnection; timings, RPC lifecycles and election rules are untouched.
Applied state is read from the MockFSM that each node runs with, filtered to the two write payloads, after the partition is healed, one further entry is committed and 300 ms have passed.
excluded: No crash, storage fault, snapshot install or log compaction is exercised.
The no-feature restart control inside the cluster remains unexecuted.

basis.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. It starts D and E, adds each as voter through the leader, applies one further command and emits 'fixture'. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome'. It then reconnects the full mesh, waits for exactly one leader, applies one further entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' with the payloads and terms at the conflict index, payload consistency, same_term_conflicting_payload, log last indexes, the restarted node's and B's configurations, the leader's configuration, the number of nodes behind the leader, each node's applied write list, whether those lists agree, and post_heal_apply_error. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft AppendEntries log-matching and the FSM apply path: same-term duplicates are skipped, so the FSM state on the two sides keeps the entries their own leader committed.

comparisons.description: After the partition is healed, every node's FSM should have applied the same commands at the index both leaders used.

semantic_changes: After the outcome sample the harness reconnects every transport pair, waits up to 15s for exactly one leader, applies one further entry on that leader and waits 300ms.

A fourth event 'healed' reports each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, whether those payloads are consistent, whether they conflict at equal terms, each node's log last index, the restarted node's configuration and each side's reported configuration, plus derived operands a_log_advanced_after_heal and nodes_with_log_behind_leader.

Three comparisons are added on the 'healed' event: entry payloads at the conflicting index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership after the cluster runs on, and its log must have advanced.

The healed event now also reports each node's applied command list (MockFSM applied data filtered to the two conflicting write payloads), whether those lists agree, and the restarted and majority nodes' applied writes.
Three comparisons are added over the healed event: the applied writes must agree across nodes, and the two operand comparisons confirming which write each side applied.

responsibility.before: hashicorp/raft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay; the AppendEntries log-matching rule (truncate only on term difference, skip same-term duplicates) is responsible for whether the divergent entries can be reconciled.
responsibility.after: hashicorp/raft AppendEntries log-matching and the FSM apply path: same-term duplicates are skipped, so the FSM state on the two sides keeps the entries their own leader committed.

before.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration while both sides lead.
After the partition heals, all nodes must hold the same entry at the index both leaders committed at.
Once the cluster is whole again and committing new entries, the restarted node must use the committed membership.
Progress control: the restarted node's log did advance after healing, so the stale membership is not a stalled state.

after.description: After the partition is healed, every node's FSM should have applied the same commands at the index both leaders used.
Operand: the restarted node's FSM applied the minority write, which the current configuration's quorum never accepted.
Operand: a node on the majority side applied the majority write at the same index.
